newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes slip in thin late trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes slip in thin late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices slipped from steady levels late Friday, tracking a West Texas Intermediate market weakened by profit-taking.
Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were unchanged as traders ceased discussion ahead of the weekend.
An industry conference also eased trade.

Outright prices for Alaskan grade eased 10 cents from midday to $22.30/22.60 a barrel, in line with November West Texas Intermediate (WTI), which fell 10 cents on a technical correction following early week price spikes.
NYMEX crude oil trimmed its recent gains by falling as much as 35 cents a barrel intraday and ending eight cents lower at $24.81.
Buyers kept bids at $2.50 Friday and said business was quiet as they squared positions for November.
One buyer discounted rumors that gasoline prices were bearish because of stockpiles at Chevron's Los Angeles-area refinery.
Supplies may be enroute over water in antipation of Chevron's immiment maintenance closure of a fluid catalytic cracker at the plant, traders said.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
